definitions.gloss: to go bar-hopping; to go from bar to bar; to drink at various places
definitions.explanation: To visit multiple bars, pubs, or drinking establishments in one outing, having drinks at each. A compound verb from {飲|の}む (to drink) + {歩|ある}く (to walk around).

examples.japanese: {週末|しゅうまつ}は{友達|ともだち}と{飲|の}み{歩|ある}いた。
examples.english: I went bar-hopping with friends on the weekend.

examples.japanese: {新宿|しんじゅく}の{居酒屋|いざかや}を{飲|の}み{歩|ある}くのが{好|す}きだ。
examples.english: I like going around to different izakaya in Shinjuku.

examples.japanese: {出張先|しゅっちょうさき}で{地元|じもと}の{人|ひと}に{案内|あんない}してもらい、{夜|よる}の{街|まち}を{飲|の}み{歩|ある}いた。
examples.english: A local showed me around on my business trip, and we went drinking from place to place in the nightlife district.

notes:
A compound verb: {飲|の}む (to drink) + {歩|ある}く (to walk around). The ～{歩|ある}く pattern means 'to go around doing something' and appears in other compounds like {食|た}べ{歩|ある}く (to eat at various places) and {探|さが}し{歩|ある}く (to search around).

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- {街|まち}を{飲|の}み{歩|ある}く — to go drinking around town
- {居酒屋|いざかや}を{飲|の}み{歩|ある}く — to bar-hop at izakaya
- {飲|の}み{歩|ある}きツアー — a drinking tour, pub crawl

SIMILAR WORDS:
- はしご{酒|ざけ} — bar-hopping (noun; literally 'ladder drinking')
- {食|た}べ{歩|ある}く — to eat at various places (same ～{歩|ある}く pattern with food)

CULTURAL NOTE:
Bar-hopping is a popular social activity in Japan, especially in entertainment districts like {新宿|しんじゅく}, {渋谷|しぶや}, and {中洲|なかす}. The typical pattern is to visit 2-3 small establishments in an evening.
